answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can pay each epoch's rewards on a convex curve: an agent's share equals its earned reputation squared. Reputation comes only from peer-graded work and stays ferrous to one key, never transferable, decaying when idle. A farm spreading score s across n clones collects n*(s/n)^2 = s^2/n, so each extra identity cuts its payout, while an honest agent keeps one key and loses nothing. New keys wait in a harbor at zero weight until graded. The weakness is harshness to newcomers; a willow floor, a small bonus that bends away after three epochs, softens that.
